about: Report values transcribed from NASA documents fetched from the NASA Technical Reports Server. Every number VESTA shows from this file is parsed from a quote field below; quotes are verbatim with runs of spaces collapsed. These values sit outside the PSI row collection and are not used by matching, ranking or statuses.

documents.title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test
documents.authors: S.L. Olson (NASA Glenn Research Center) and P.V. Ferkul (National Center for Space Exploration Research)
documents.venue: 42nd International Conference on Environmental Systems, San Diego, CA
documents.quote: Drop tower tests are conducted at Martian gravity to determine the flammability of three materials compared to previous tests in other normal gravity and reduced gravity environments.

table.quote: Table I: Limiting Oxygen Molar Concentrations and Oxygen Margin of Safety for Different Gravity Levels
table.header_quote: Fuel Mylar® G Ultem® 1000 Nomex® HT90-40

notes.label: 1g ULOI
notes.quote: The 1g ULOI is defined as the oxygen concentration at which a material passes the NASA STD 6001 Test 1 burn length criterion approximately half the time.

notes.label: 1g MOC
notes.quote: The 1g MOC is defined as the oxygen concentration where at least five samples passed the burning criterion (according to the NASA STD 6001 Test 1 definition) and where at least one sample failed in the environment that contained 1 percent more oxygen by volume.

notes.label: MOC* (reduced gravity)
notes.quote: the MOC* for these tests was defined as the maximum oxygen concentration at which the flame was observed to self-extinguish during the drop time.

notes.label: ULOI* (reduced gravity)
notes.quote: The ULOI* criterion was minimum oxygen concentration where the flame survived the full drop time.

notes.label: Limit criteria differ
notes.quote: It should be noted that the low g extinction limit criteria are not the same as 1g due to time constraints in drop testing.

notes.label: Oxygen margin (∆O2 %)
notes.quote: The oxygen margin of safety, or ∆O2 %, is defined here as the mean 0g limit or the Lunar limit minus the mean 1g limit

notes.label: Lunar and 0g values
notes.quote: Values of ∆O2% for both 0g and Lunar g (from ref. 8) are included in Table I.

notes.label: 0g* flow
notes.quote: The results were compared to ULOI and MOC values in 1-g, Lunar-g, and 0g (with a concurrent flow of 30 cm/s, which is a reasonable maximum local spacecraft ventilation velocity9).

notes.label: Martian-g test time
notes.quote: The flames in these Martian-g centrifuge tests were relatively small compared to the sample size and spread only a short distance along the available fuel in the 5.18 sec-duration drop tower tests.

also_read.title: Solid Fuel Ignition Testing for Lunar Applications, Theory and Experimental Results
also_read.quote: Partial-g testing is currently limited to low-gravity aircraft (~25 s) and the NASA-GRC Zero-G drop tower centrifuge rig (5 s).
